perspective:
Angela Hwang’s available information:

- She knows Kevin Flores is her long-time friend since high school, and they confide in each other.
- At the coffee meeting, she invited Kevin. She heard him say he had been “alright” with the usual work grind, then admit he was unhappy, felt stuck and unfulfilled, and was just going through the motions. She heard him say he had thought about changing jobs/careers but did not know where to start and felt overwhelmed. She told him she was worried, suggested a different job or career path, and offered to explore options together. Kevin agreed.
- She later found job openings and a career counseling service. She told Kevin about them. She heard Kevin thank her and say he had been thinking a lot, was interested in something more creative, and mentioned design or architecture. She encouraged him to check the resources. He said he would.
- She believed Kevin was hesitant about making a career change and felt frustrated and worried. She arranged a meeting with a career coach and told Kevin. She heard him say she didn’t have to do that, that he appreciated it, but he was not sure he was ready. She encouraged him to take a small push. He agreed to give it a shot and thanked her.
- She believed Kevin was making progress and felt proud and relieved. She asked how things were going with the career coach. She heard Kevin say the coach had been helpful, he had started online courses in design, and he felt more confident. She offered further help. He said just knowing she was there was enough, and he would tell her if he needed anything.
- She believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career and felt happy and satisfied. She organized a small celebration party and told him. She heard Kevin thank her, say he was grateful, and say he couldn’t have done it without her. She told him he did the hard work and suggested they enjoy the party. He agreed.
